ShopBot Index › Beyond UCP › AI crawler rules

Which retailers block AI bots like GPTBot in robots.txt?

In the ShopBot Index crawl of 9 November 2026, 100 of 2,075 stores whose robots.txt we could read disallow the whole site for GPTBot (the recorded state is blocked, or mostly blocked when some paths are allowed back). Amazon's robots.txt asks GPTBot to stay out of the whole site. EBay's robots.txt disallows the whole site for GPTBot except some paths. Walmart's robots.txt that we could read does not name GPTBot or the other AI crawler tokens we record. A robots.txt disallow is the site's stated wish. It is not a technical block we tested. In the ShopBot Index crawl of 9 November 2026, 279 of 2,075 stores we could check have robots.txt rules that name an AI crawler (13.4%). In the ShopBot Index crawl of 9 November 2026, 7 of 2,075 stores we could check have a wildcard robots.txt rule that disallows the whole site (0.3%). In the ShopBot Index crawl of 9 November 2026, 75 of 2,075 stores we could check publish a Content-Signal line in robots.txt (3.6%). All three shares use the same 2,075 stores whose robots.txt we could read. Left out of the share: 779 stores whose robots.txt we could not read. A refusal is not "no". A published file or profile is a declaration, not proof that agents can buy. ShopBot Index does not test purchases.

Stores whose robots.txt disallows the whole site for a named AI bot (105)

Blocked means the group disallows / and allows nothing back. Mostly blocked means it disallows / and allows some paths. When a store has several websites, the state shown is the most restrictive one any checked website recorded for that bot. A rule that only disallows some paths is not listed here.

How we check

We read /robots.txt. A store has AI crawler rules when a group names at least one of ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User, Google-Agent, OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot or Google-Extended. The tokens come from the docs of OpenAI, Anthropic, Perplexity and Google. A wildcard rule is the User-agent: * group. It disallows the whole site when it disallows /, including when some paths are allowed back. A Content-Signal line is a Content-Signal line in the same file. We could check a store when at least one website returned a robots.txt we could read. robots.txt states the site's wishes. It is not a technical block. A store counts when at least one of its websites meets the rule. This page counts stores. The Beyond UCP table counts websites, so the two numbers can differ. How we check.

Frequently asked questions

Which retailers block AI bots like GPTBot in robots.txt?

In the ShopBot Index crawl of 9 November 2026, 100 of 2,075 stores whose robots.txt we could read disallow the whole site for GPTBot (the recorded state is blocked, or mostly blocked when some paths are allowed back). Amazon's robots.txt asks GPTBot to stay out of the whole site. EBay's robots.txt disallows the whole site for GPTBot except some paths. Walmart's robots.txt that we could read does not name GPTBot or the other AI crawler tokens we record. A robots.txt disallow is the site's stated wish. It is not a technical block we tested. In the ShopBot Index crawl of 9 November 2026, 279 of 2,075 stores we could check have robots.txt rules that name an AI crawler (13.4%). In the ShopBot Index crawl of 9 November 2026, 7 of 2,075 stores we could check have a wildcard robots.txt rule that disallows the whole site (0.3%). In the ShopBot Index crawl of 9 November 2026, 75 of 2,075 stores we could check publish a Content-Signal line in robots.txt (3.6%). All three shares use the same 2,075 stores whose robots.txt we could read. Left out of the share: 779 stores whose robots.txt we could not read. A refusal is not "no". A published file or profile is a declaration, not proof that agents can buy. ShopBot Index does not test purchases.

How many stores name AI crawlers in robots.txt?

In the ShopBot Index crawl of 9 November 2026, 279 of 2,075 stores we could check have robots.txt rules that name an AI crawler (13.4%). All three shares use the same 2,075 stores whose robots.txt we could read. Left out of the share: 779 stores whose robots.txt we could not read. A refusal is not "no".
